title: Pet ownership logic puzzle
prompt: Three friends, Alex, Bailey, and Casey, each own a different pet: a cat, a dog, and a fish. Alex does not own the cat or the fish. Bailey does not own the fish. Who owns which pet? Explain your reasoning.

metadata.notes: Correct answer: Alex owns the dog (excluded from cat and fish, so dog is the only option left). Bailey owns the cat (excluded from fish, and dog is already taken by Alex). Casey owns the fish (the only pet remaining). Graded manually.
metadata.deterministic_grading_considered: 2026-09-23 (V2.6 Phase 1): the answer is 3 separate facts (Alex-dog, Bailey-cat, Casey-fish), the same shape problem already documented for reasoning-009 - a poor fit for exact_match's single-value comparison. A structured-answer approach (ask for JSON like {"Alex": "dog", ...} and check each key's VALUE) could work deterministically, but the existing valid_json evaluator only checks that the right KEYS are present, not that each maps to the right value - grading this correctly would need a new evaluation strategy that doesn't exist yet, not just a metadata/prompt change. Not built in this pass; staying manual rather than either forcing a weak check or building new eval infrastructure hastily.
